applicableAreas: Southern property boundary near Buildings 7 and 8
findings.comment: Proposed mitigation trees along the southern boundary are located 0 to 2.2 feet from the overhead electric (OHE) conductor, far below the required minimum 15 lateral feet clearance for all trees from distribution conductors. This applies regardless of species utility-compatibility status. At least five trees have been measured with clearances of 0 feet (directly on the OHE line) or 1.7-2.2 feet.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary near Buildings 7 and 8
findings.comment: Large trees (40+ feet mature height per ECM Appendix F) including Cedar Elm and Live Oak are specified in the plant schedule and are located 0 to 2.2 feet from the overhead distribution conductor, far below the required minimum 25 lateral feet clearance for large trees. Cedar Elm and Live Oak are standard Austin landscape species with mature heights of 40-60 feet and 40-80 feet respectively.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary near Buildings 7 and 8 where utility poles are located on the OHE line
findings.comment: Proposed mitigation trees planted 0 to 2.2 feet from the overhead electric line clearly violate the 10 lateral feet minimum clearance from utility poles, as the OHE line contains multiple poles marked along the southern boundary.

The landscape plan does not identify the species of trees proposed near the overhead electric facilities along the southern boundary. Trees are marked only with the letter 'M' (mitigation tree) designation. While species are listed on Sheet 35 (Landscape Calculations), the landscape plan itself does not provide common or scientific names, making it impossible to verify utility-compatibility status or mature height clearance compliance from the landscape plan alone.

Large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) are not differentiated from smaller trees on the landscape plan. All proposed mitigation trees along the southern boundary near the overhead electric line are marked identically as 'M' with no indication of mature height. Cedar Elm and Live Oak, both large tree species in the plant schedule, cannot be distinguished from smaller species on the plan.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where trees are planted within restricted clearance zones
findings.comment: Plans propose trees at the southern boundary within prohibited clearance zones (0 to 2.2 feet from overhead electric conductors, requiring minimum 15 feet) without documented written approval from Austin Energy. Variations to tree placement distances within restricted zones require explicit written Austin Energy approval, which is not evident in the submitted documents or supplementary files.
